correctness.rationale: Convexity of ||P-J/N|| and leaf-class automorphisms reduce global optimum to three symmetric weights a,b,c. At candidate both hub row constraints saturate, quotient 4x4 Laplacian polynomial has factors z(z-c)[z²-(2+a)z+(p+q+2)ab]; leaf differences have eigenvalues a or c. Factor sign bounds place other nonzero eigenvalues inside (c,2-c), hence SLEM=1-c=q²/(q²+q-p). A candidate quotient Rayleigh witness x and the right-leaf difference eigenvalue yield an affine-max lower support F; positive Lagrange multipliers exist iff H_{p,q}>=0, proving global optimum. If H<0, decreasing the bridge weight while preserving hub saturation lowers both active eigenbranches and hence SLEM. H(q) strictly increases with unique zero in (2p,3p), with asymptotic ratio 1+sqrt2. Independent direct symmetric-matrix eigenvalues and local improvements for 6 configurations corroborated certificates.
residual_risks: The exact quotient factorization and dual gradient are the essential nonstandard calculations; finite numerical checks are corroboration, not proof for all integers.
Claim only classifies global optimum on q>=Q_p; below this it shows candidate strictly suboptimal but not true optimizer; uniqueness only invariant optimizers for q>Q_p.
